what_this_is: The Workshop row for the settings folder: the one reader every Workshop tool uses to read the settings a person keeps for it as rows of their list:settings, by person, film, piece or account.

payload.label: Read the settings a person keeps for a tool, for one person, film, piece or their whole account (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Read the settings a person keeps for one of their tools, choosing the row for this piece, else this film, else this person, else their whole account, or make the settings row to write
payload.description: A tool's settings are rows of the person's list:settings (record:setting:<workshop-folder>~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>; fields name, tool, scope_kind, scope_id, settings as JSON, from, status). read: give the records records:read returned (or the path of the file holding them), the tool's folder and the scopes to try, most specific first; the answer is the settings of the first scope that has an active row, or the default given when none does. make: give the folder, scope, settings, name, tool and where the values came from; the answer is the record records:write takes, with the list:settings record when asked. The same reader is a library for Python (read-data/settings.py) and JavaScript (read-data/settings.mjs) tools.

settings_record.description: A record:setting as records:read gives it, its value, a list of them, or the path of a JSON file holding them.

folder.description: The Workshop folder whose settings to read, e.g. make-a-frame-contact-sheet-of-a-video-section.

default.description: What to answer when no row matches.

tool.description: Refuse a row written for another tool.

make.description: {folder, scope_kind, scope_id, settings, name, tool, from, status?}: make the row instead of reading one.

output_schema.description: The last line printed: {"result": {found, id, settings}} for read, {"result": {records}} for make; {"error": ...} with exit 2 when the request cannot be read.

invoke.say: Read the person's list:settings rows for the tool through their records door (records:list on list:settings, or records:read of record:setting:<folder>~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>), write them to a file, and pass that file as settings_record with the folder and the scopes to try. A tool that takes settings_record in its own request reads it with read-data/settings.py or read-data/settings.mjs itself.

provenance.source: Ported from old Trillion's setting record kind: Trillion-X/trillion src/decision-store.mjs before 4ffa1dc4a2, lines 8 and 751-754 (setting(name) gives the value or null; setSetting writes { id: setting:<name>, type: setting }).
